format.note: each tournament is a 22-round double round-robin and crowns its own champion from its own table; no play-off, no points carried between the two; our row is the Clausura half of a 44-match season

boundaries.note: Intermedia champion and runner-up are promoted directly. The two worst three-season points-per-game averages in the top flight are relegated, regardless of the single-season table (Rubio Ñu and San Lorenzo went down in 2026). No play-offs in either direction.

notes: Both 2026 seasons are complete. 12 clubs at level 1, 16 at level 2, matching our rows. Level 1 runs two championships (Apertura and Clausura) of 22 rounds each; each crowns its own champion, no play-off, no points carried, and a separate aggregate table is used only for the relegation average and Libertadores seeding. Relegation from the top flight is decided by a three-season points-per-game average (tabla de descenso): two clubs go down, which is why promoted clubs Rubio Núu and San Lorenzo were relegated again in the same season. División Intermedia: 30 rounds, champion and runner-up promoted directly, three clubs relegated on the same three-season average, with the destination split by geography between Primera B Metropolitana and Primera B Nacional (tier 3, not modelled, hence closed_down for PAR2). No promotion or relegation play-offs anywhere in this pyramid.
